title: The James Derivation — Smyrna → James, executable

elements.name: superscription
elements.greek: ho prōtos kai ho eschatos, hos egeneto nekros kai ezēsen
elements.quote: These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive

elements.name: tribulation-knowledge
elements.quote: I know thy works, and tribulation
elements.gloss: the assembly's suffering, known and named

elements.name: poverty–riches inversion
elements.gloss: four words: material poverty, actual wealth

elements.name: the claim that is not
elements.greek: tēn blasphēmian ek tōn legontōn Ioudaious einai heautous, kai ouk eisin
elements.quote: the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not
elements.gloss: an identity said and not had; the saying is blasphemy. The same formula at Ephesus (2:2) and Philadelphia (3:9)

elements.name: contested synagōgē
elements.quote: but are the synagogue of Satan
elements.gloss: a fight over who the assembly is, and over the word for it

elements.name: imprisonment-as-testing
elements.quote: the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried
elements.gloss: trial with an agent and a purpose

elements.name: bounded tribulation
elements.quote: ye shall have tribulation ten days
elements.gloss: suffering with a term set on it

elements.name: fidelity imperative
elements.gloss: the command: endurance to the end

elements.name: crown promise (performative)
elements.greek: dōsō soi ton stephanon tēs zōēs
elements.quote: and I will give thee a crown of life
elements.gloss: first-person FUTURE — the promise being made

elements.name: hearing formula
elements.greek: ho echōn ous akousatō ti to pneuma legei tais ekklēsiais
elements.quote: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches
elements.gloss: the reception imperative; it closes every one of the seven letters

elements.name: overcomer formula
elements.greek: ou mē adikēthē ek tou thanatou tou deuterou
elements.quote: He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death
elements.gloss: death has an economy; overcoming exempts

seed.note: Elements are listed in the order of the text; IDs S1–S9 are the v1.0 IDs, kept.

rules.gloss: unfold the sender-formula into a letter opening: named position + diaspora address
unfold the event of trial into a theology of peirasmos: its joy, its product, its true agency
the promise made in the seed is cited in the unfolding as already-given: dōsō → epēngeilato
unfold the four-word poverty–riches inversion into a doctrine of the poor and a judgment of the rich
the word fought over in the seed is simply used in the unfolding, without argument
suffering-with-a-term becomes stories of patience: the farmer, the prophets, Job
the second death unfolds into a full account of how death is produced and escaped
one imperative becomes an ethics: endurance made complete, wanting nothing
the seed's 'say they are, and are not' becomes a procedure for testing what anyone says they are or have: faith said and not had, religion seemed and not kept

emissions.produces: Prescript: a named position writing to the scattered assembly

matches.greek: tais dōdeka phylais tais en tē diaspora
matches.quote: James… to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting
matches.note: the diaspora address — the assembly Smyrna's letter fights for, written to as a whole

emissions.produces: Doctrine of testing: trial has a product and a true agency

matches.greek: to dokimion hymōn tēs pisteōs katergazetai hypomonēn
matches.quote: count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience
matches.note: peirasmos theologized: the seed's hina peirasthēte given its purpose-clause in full

matches.greek: mēdeis peirazomenos legetō hoti apo theou peirazomai
matches.quote: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God
matches.note: agency refined: the seed's devil-agency answered with a doctrine of where testing comes from

matches.greek: lēmpsetai ton stephanon tēs zōēs, hon epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton
matches.quote: he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him
matches.note: THE ARROW IN THE MORPHOLOGY: Rev 2:10 performs the promise (dōsō, first-person future); Jas 1:12 cites it (epēngeilato, aorist — promised, past). The only two occurrences of ton stephanon tēs zōēs in the canon. The epistle receipts the letter.

matches.greek: klēronomous tēs basileias hēs epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton
matches.quote: heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him
matches.note: the receipt clause of 1:12 a second time, word for word, now on the kingdom — in the verse that also carries the poverty–riches inversion (S3) and the hearing imperative (S11)

emissions.produces: Social theology: the poor elected, the rich withering, the rich as persecutors

matches.greek: tous ptōchous tō kosmō plousious en pistei
matches.quote: Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom
matches.note: the seed's inversion, verbatim in its terms: ptōchos become plousios

matches.greek: helkousin hymas eis kritēria … blasphēmousin to kalon onoma
matches.quote: Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats? Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
matches.note: the seed's custody and blasphemy given to the rich: ballein … eis phylakēn (the devil, into prison) → helkousin … eis kritēria (the rich, into courts); blasphēmian (2:9) → blasphēmousin, the only blasphēm- in James

matches.quote: let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted: but the rich, in that he is made low
Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries
matches.note: the judgment side of the inversion, fully unfolded

matches.quote: if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring
matches.note: synagōgē for the believing assembly — alone among the epistles. The seed's contested word, held without polemic.

matches.quote: Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth… be ye also patient
matches.note: endurance with a term: the ten days become the season until the rain

matches.quote: Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord
matches.note: bounded suffering narrativized — the trial that ends

matches.quote: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death
matches.note: how the death of the formula is produced

matches.quote: shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins
matches.note: and how it is escaped — the epistle closes where the seed's promise pointed

emissions.produces: Paraenesis: endurance made complete; hearing made doing

matches.quote: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing
matches.note: the fidelity imperative unfolded into the epistle's whole ethic

matches.greek: ginesthe de poiētai logou kai mē akroatai monon
matches.quote: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only
matches.note: the fidelity imperative's own verb, ginou → ginesthe, joined to the hearing formula: 'become faithful' + 'let him hear' → 'become doers of the word, not hearers only'

matches.greek: tachys eis to akousai … ouk akroatēs epilēsmonēs … alla poiētēs ergou
matches.quote: let every man be swift to hear … he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed
matches.note: the hearing formula unfolded into its process: hear, look into the law, continue, do, be blessed

matches.greek: ean pistin legē tis echein erga de mē echē
matches.quote: though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?
matches.note: legontōn … einai … kai ouk eisin → legē tis echein … mē echē: the saying, and the not-having, in the same order

matches.quote: If any man among you seem to be religious … this man's religion is vain
matches.note: the claimed identity (einai) tested against conduct

morphological_arrow.seed: dōsō soi (I will give — first-person future, the promise performed)
morphological_arrow.unfolding: hon epēngeilato (which he promised — aorist, the promise cited)
morphological_arrow.claim: the direction of dependency is visible in the verb forms: performance, then receipt

sapiential material without a Smyrna source

slate.note: The seven-letter evaluation slate (2026-07-28): best epistle and heteronym position per letter, graded by evidence hardness — unique shared collocations, then structural knots, then canonical mechanisms, then themes. Grades are the evaluation's, offered for ruling, not settled canon.

rows.evidence: 'first love' ↔ the commandment ap' archēs (1 Jn 2:7); 'tried them which say they are apostles' ↔ 'try the spirits' (4:1); antichrists who went out. Note: 'in Ephesus' absent from the earliest MSS of Ephesians — the nominal mapping is the weak one.

crown of life — unique pair in the canon; synagōgē possessed (Jas 2:2, alone among epistles); ptōchos/plousios inversion; peirasmos→dokimos architecture; the dōsō→epēngeilato arrow, twice (1:12, 2:5); the Jas 2:2–7 knot. THE GRANULAR CASE, below.

the triple knot: eidōlothyta + Balaam's Peor-fornication (1 Cor 10:8 = Num 25) + manna typology (10:3), one pericope; stumbling-block term; white stone's new name shadowing the renamed apostle; Satan's throne = the imperial seat. Transform class: ADVERSARIAL unfolding — the letter condemns what the epistle permits.

Lydia of Thyatira, seller of purple, founds Philippi's assembly (Acts 16:14); morning star ↔ phōstēres (Phil 2:15); works, love, service, faith, patience ↔ the partnership letter. Mediated through Acts.
the thief (Rev 3:3 ↔ 1 Thess 5:2) and watch/sleep (grēgoreō ↔ 1 Thess 5:6); a name that lives while dead ↔ them which are asleep. Shared collocations, not unique ones.

peri de tēs philadelphias, 'ye need not that I write unto you' (1 Thess 4:9) — a meta-statement about writing to Philadelphia; hē philadelphia menetō (Heb 13:1); the open door as epistolary idiom (1 Cor 16:9; 2 Cor 2:12). Split evidence.

Col 4:16 names the exchange — 'the epistle from Laodicea'; hē archē tēs ktiseōs (Rev 3:14) ↔ prōtotokos pasēs ktiseōs… archē (Col 1:15,18); riches answered to 'them at Laodicea' by name (Col 2:1–3); white raiment ↔ the put-off/put-on clothing program (Col 3). The canonical-mechanism case: the canon itself records the exchange.
